title: Example
body_md:
In the framework of the composite optimization problem \eqref{comp}, let $\varphi(x)=-x-\frac12x^2$, $\Phi(x)=x$ for $x\in {\mathbb R}$, and $g(z)=z+\delta_{{\mathbb R}_-}(z)$ for $z\in{\mathbb R}$. 
Set ${\bar{x}}=0$, $\bar{y}=1$, and $\bar{z} := \Phi({\bar{x}}) = 0$. We get $\partial g(0)=[1,+\infty)$ and observe that $\bar y\in\partial g(\bar{z})$ but $\bar y\notin {\rm ri}\,\partial g(\bar{z})$.
The Lagrangian, corresponding to this composite problem,  is $ L(x,y)=-x-\frac12x^2+xy$.
Thus, $\nabla_xL(x,y)=-1-x+y$ and $\nabla_xL(0,1)=0$. 
Combining these tells us that $({\bar{x}},\bar{y})$ is a solution to the associated KKT system in \eqref{vs}. 
On the other hand, the critical cone of $g$ at $\bar{z}$ for $\bar{y}$ is
$K_g(0,1)=N_{\partial g(0)}(1)={\mathbb R}_-$, which implies that 
$$
    {\rm d}^2g(0,1)(w)=\delta_{K_g(0,1)}(w)= \delta_{{\mathbb R}_-}(w)\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad D(\partial g)(0,1)(w)=N_{{\mathbb R}_-}(w)
$$
for any $w\in {\mathbb R}$. Since $\nabla^2_{xx}L(0,1)=-1$ and 
    $\nabla\Phi(0)=1$, the condition \eqref{crc} reads as 
    $$
     0\in -w+N_{{\mathbb R}_-}(w).
    $$
It is not hard to see that  the only solution to this inclusion is $w=0$, and therefore $\bar y=1$ is a noncritical multiplier. 
Observe that the Lagrange multiplier set at ${\bar{x}}$ is $\Lambda({\bar{x}})=\{1\}$.
Define 
\begin{equation*}
 \sigma(x,y):=|x|+|y-1|=|x|+{\rm dist}(y,\Lambda({\bar{x}})), \quad (x, y) \in {\mathbb R}^2.
\end{equation*} 
It is clear that $\sigma$ satisfies the two-sided error bound estimates in \eqref{eb} with constants  $\kappa_1=\kappa_2=1$. 

Set 
$x_t=0$ and  $y_t=1+t$ for $t\in (0,1)$. 
We then have $\sigma(x_t,y_t)=t$.  
We will show that both variational systems \eqref{au-KKT} and \eqref{ssqp-kkt} fail to have a solution with $(x,y)=(x_t,y_t)$ for any $ t\in (0,1)$. The first equation in both variational systems becomes
$0=-1-s+q$, which results in $q = s +1$. 
The second inclusion in the auxiliary system \eqref{au-KKT} reads as
$q-\bar y\in N_{{\mathbb R}_-}\big(s-t(q-y_t)\big)$. 
Substituting $\bar y=1$, $y_t=1+t$, and $q = s + 1$, we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{eq:poly-core}
    s\in N_{{\mathbb R}_-}\big((1-t)s+t^2\big).
\end{equation}
Set $r:=(1-t)s+t^2$. If $r<0$, we deduce from \eqref{eq:poly-core} that $s=0$, which results in $r=t^2>0$, a contradiction. If  $r=0$, then $s=-{t^2}/{(1-t)}<0$. However, \eqref{eq:poly-core} would require that $s\ge 0$, which is not possible. Finally, if $r>0$, then \eqref{eq:poly-core} cannot be fulfilled. 
Thus, the auxiliary system \eqref{au-KKT} has no solution with $(x, y) = (x_t,y_t)$ for any $t\in (0,1)$.

To show that the same conclusion holds for \eqref{ssqp-kkt}, we conclude from $q=s+1$ and $r=(1-t)s+t^2$ that the inclusion in \eqref{ssqp-kkt} becomes 
\begin{equation}\label{sikkt}
q\in \partial g (r).
\end{equation} If $r<0$, we deduce from $\partial g(r)=\{1\}$ that  $s+1=1$. Thus,  $s=0$, which gives $r=t^2>0$, a contradiction.  If $r=0$, we get $s=-{t^2}/{(1-t)}<0$ and therefore $q=s+1<1$.
In this case, it follows from $\partial g(0)=[1,\infty)$ that $q\notin\partial g(0)$, a contradiction with \eqref{sikkt}.  If $r>0$, we clearly have $\partial g(r)=\emptyset$.  Thus, \eqref{ssqp-kkt} has no solution with $(x,y)=(x_t,y_t)$ for any $t\in (0,1)$.

title: Example
body_md:
Consider the composite optimization problem \eqref{comp} with $\varphi(x)=-\frac12x^2$, $\Phi(x)=x$ for $x\in {\mathbb R}$, and
  $$
  g(z) = \begin{cases}
    0 & \mbox{if}\;\; z\le 0,\\      
    z^2 & \mbox{if}\;\; z> 0.
    \end{cases}
 $$
 Clearly, $g$ is a CPLQ function but is not polyhedral.
 Let $\bar x=\bar y=0$. Then $\bar z:=\Phi(\bar x)=0$ and $\bar{y}\in \partial g(\bar{z})=\{0\}$.
 The Lagrangian of this problem takes the form $L(x,y)=-\frac12x^2+xy$, and hence $ \nabla_xL(x,y)=-x+y$. Since $\nabla_xL({\bar{x}},\bar{y})=0$, we conclude that $({\bar{x}},\bar{y})$ is a KKT point.
 The second subderivative of $g$ at $\bar{z}$ for $\bar{y}$ is given by 
$$
    h(w):={\rm d}^2g(\bar{z},\bar{y})(w)=
    \begin{cases}
    0 & \mbox{if}\;\; w\le 0,\\      
    2w^2 & \mbox{if}\;\; w>0,
    \end{cases}
$$ 
which in turn yields
$$
D(\partial g)(\bar{z},\bar{y})(w)=\partial \Big(\frac{1}{2}{\rm d}^2g(\bar{z},\bar{y})\Big)(w)= \begin{cases}
    \{0\} & \mbox{if}\;\; w\le 0,\\      
    \{2w\} & \mbox{if}\;\; w>0.
    \end{cases}
$$
The inclusion in \eqref{crc} then takes the form 
\[
    0\in \nabla^2_{xx}L({\bar{x}},\bar{y})w+D(\partial g)(\bar{z},\bar{y})(w)
   =\begin{cases}
    \{-w\} & \mbox{if}\;\; w\le 0,\\      
    \{w\} & \mbox{if}\;\; w>0.
    \end{cases}
\]
If $w<0$, this gives $0=-w$, which is not possible.    
If $w>0$, it gives $0=w$, again a contradiction. 
The latter inclusion clearly holds for $w = 0$.
Thus the only solution of this inclusion is $w=0$, meaning that $\bar y$ is a noncritical Lagrange multiplier.
Moreover, the Lagrange multiplier set at ${\bar{x}}$ is given by $\Lambda({\bar{x}})=\{0\}$.
Define 
$$  
\sigma(x,y):=|x|+|y|=|x|+{\rm dist}(y,\Lambda({\bar{x}})), \quad (x, y) \in {\mathbb R}^2.
$$
It can be seen that $\sigma$ satisfies the two-sided error bound estimates in \eqref{eb} with constants  $\kappa_1=\kappa_2=1$. 

Set
$x_t=0$ and  $y_t=t$ for $t\in (0,1/2)$. We then get 
 $\sigma(x_t,y_t)=t$.  We will show that both variational systems \eqref{au-KKT} and \eqref{ssqp-kkt} fail to have a solution with $(x,y)=(x_t,y_t)$ for any $t\in (0, 1/2)$. The first equation in both variational systems takes the form
$0=-s+q$, which yields $s=q$. Set $r:=(1-t)s+t^2$. The second inclusion in the auxiliary system \eqref{au-KKT} then reads as
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cplq-core}
    s\in \frac12\partial h(r).
\end{equation}
Suppose that $r\le0$.  Since  $\partial h(r)=\{0\}$, it follows from  \eqref{eq:cplq-core} that $s=0$, which yields $r=t^2>0$, a contradiction.  If $r>0$, we deduce from \eqref{eq:cplq-core} that $s=2r=2((1-t)s+t^2)$. This leads to $r = s/2={t^2}/{(2t-1)}<0$ due to  $t\in (0,1/2)$,
which contradicts $r>0$.  Thus the auxiliary system has no solution with $(x, y) =(x_t,y_t)$ for any $t\in (0,1/2)$. 

To justify the same conclusion for \eqref{ssqp-kkt}, we observe first that 
$$
\partial g(z)=
    \begin{cases}
    \{0\} & \mbox{if}\;\; z\le 0,\\      
    \{2z\} & \mbox{if}\;\; z>0.
    \end{cases}
$$
Thus, the inclusion $q\in\partial g(r)$ in \eqref{ssqp-kkt}, together with $q=s$  and $r=(1-t)s+t^2$, leads us to the same cases as those of the auxiliary system,  discussed above.  Therefore, the variational system \eqref{ssqp-kkt} has no solution with $(x,y)=(x_t,y_t)$ whenever $t\in(0,1/2)$.

label: prop:eb2
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:eb2}
Let $({\bar{x}}, \bar{y})$ be a solution to the KKT system \eqref{vs} with $g$ being a polyhedral function. 
Assume that $\bar{y}\in {\rm ri}\, \partial g(\Phi({\bar{x}}))$ is noncritical and $\sigma$ satisfies both error bound estimates in \eqref{eb}.
Then there exist positive constants $\varepsilon$ and $\kappa$ such that for all $(x, y)\in \mathbb{B}_\varepsilon({\bar{x}}, \bar{y})$ with $\sigma(x, y)>0$, the error bound estimate \eqref{eb3} holds for any solution $(s, q)$ to the system \eqref{au-KKT}.

label: s8.1
title: Proof
body_md:
Assume by contradiction that the estimate \eqref{eb3} fails. 
Recall the equivalent form \eqref{eq:linear} of \eqref{au-KKT} when $g$ is a polyhedral function and $\bar{y}\in {\rm ri}\, \partial g(\Phi({\bar{x}}))$.
Then there exist sequences $({x^k}, y^k)\to ({\bar{x}}, \bar{y})$, with $\sigma_k:= \sigma({x^k}, y^k)>0$, and $(s^k, q^k)$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{s8.1}
\|s^k-{x^k}\|+\|q^k-y^k\|>k \sigma_k,
\end{equation}
where $(s^k, q^k)$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{s9.1}
    0=\nabla\varphi({x^k})+ {H_k}(s^k-{x^k})+\nabla\Phi({x^k})^*q^k, \quad z^k - \bar{z} \in K, \quad q^k - \bar{y} \in K^\bot,
\end{equation}
where ${H_k} := \nabla^2_{xx}L({x^k}, y^k)$, $z^k :
= \Phi({x^k})+\nabla\Phi({x^k})(s^k-{x^k})-\sigma_k(q^k-y^k)$, $\bar{z} := \Phi({\bar{x}})$, and $K := K_g(\bar{z}, \bar{y})$.
Set $\beta_k := \|s^k-{x^k}\|+\|q^k-y^k\|$ and $\hat y^k := P_{{\Lambda}({\bar{x}})}(y^k)$.
Repeating the arguments leading to \eqref{s12} and \eqref{s16} in the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:eb}, which do not employ SOSC \eqref{sosc}, we get
\begin{equation}\label{s12.1}
0=\nabla^2_{xx}L({\bar{x}}, \bar{y})u+\nabla\Phi({\bar{x}})^*w,
\quad 
\nabla\Phi({\bar{x}})u\in K
\end{equation}
where $(u, w)\neq 0$ is defined similarly as in \eqref{s11}.
We now claim that $w\in K^\bot$.
Recall first that $\hat y^k, \bar{y}\in\partial g(\bar{z})$ and $\hat y^k \to \bar{y}$ as $k \to\infty$. The reduction relation in \eqref{rl2}, together with \eqref{pwfor2}, then yields $\hat y^k - \bar{y} \in K_g(\bar{z}, \bar{y})^* = K^\bot$. Combining this with the last inclusion in \eqref{s9.1} leads us to
\begin{equation*}
    \frac{q^k - y^k}{\beta_k} - \frac{\hat y^k - y^k}{\beta_k}= \frac{q^k - \bar{y}}{\beta_k} - \frac{\hat y^k - \bar{y}}{\beta_k}   \in  K^\bot.
\end{equation*}
Passing through the limit as $k\to\infty$ and recalling that $\|y^k - \hat y^k\| = o(\beta_k)$, as in \eqref{s10}, we arrive at $w \in K^\bot$, which proves our claim.
This, combined with \eqref{s12.1} and noncriticality of $\bar{y}$, implies that $u=0$. 
The first equality in \eqref{s12.1} then implies that $\nabla\Phi({\bar{x}})^*w=0$. 

Arguing similarly to the second half of the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:eb}, we end up with $w =0$, which is not possible. This  completes the proof.

title: Proof
body_md:
As shown in the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:calm}, the error bound estimates in \eqref{subr3} imply the local representation of ${\mathcal S}(0, 0)$ in \eqref{calm1}.
This tells us that
\begin{equation*}
    {\rm dist}((x, y), {\mathcal S}(0, 0)) = \|x - {\bar{x}}\| + {\rm dist}(y, {\Lambda}({\bar{x}}))
\end{equation*}
for all $(x, y)$ close to $({\bar{x}}, \bar{y})$.
By the arguments at the end of Subsection~\ref{sect:fischer} and by the upper bound   in \eqref{eb}, we know that the estimate in \eqref{pre} holds for all $(\tilde{x}, \tilde{y})$ sufficiently close to $({\bar{x}}, \bar{y})$ and all $(x, y)$ satisfying \eqref{pre2}.
The proof is then complete.

title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $({\bar{x}}, \bar{y})$ be a solution to the KKT system \eqref{vs} such that the SOSC \eqref{sosc} holds at $({\bar{x}}, \bar{y})$ and  $\sigma$ satisfy both error bound estimates in \eqref{eb}. 
If $(x^0, y^0)$ is chosen sufficiently close to $({\bar{x}}, \bar{y})$, then the sSQP iterates $\{({x^k}, y^k)\}_{k\in {\rm I\!N}}$ generated by Algorithm~{\rm \ref{algo:sSQP}} are well-defined and converge  to $({\bar{x}}, \hat y)$ for some $\hat y \in \Lambda({\bar{x}})$. Moreover, the rate of convergence is Q-superlinear.

The same conclusion holds when the SOSC is replaced with the noncriticality of the Lagrange multiplier $\bar{y}$, provided that $\bar{y}\in {\rm ri}\, \partial g(\Phi({\bar{x}}))$ and $g$ is a polyhedral function.
